derivation:
First-principles analysis shows the statement fails on two fundamental grounds:

(1) Empirical equivalence on a finite set does not imply functional equivalence: Two neural networks can produce identical outputs on w constraint points while differing on the rest of the input space. A counterexample constructed with ReLU networks shows a 1-unit and a 2-unit network both satisfying f(0)=0, yet producing different outputs at x=0.5, x=-0.5, etc. Since they differ functionally, they cannot be reparameterizations of each other.

(2) Dimensionality mismatch: For a network with d parameters and w independent constraints, the solution space has dimension d-w (typically large). Reparameterization symmetries form a much lower-dimensional subgroup (e.g., at most O(d) for ReLU scaling/permutation symmetries). Most solutions in the (d)-dimensional parameter space that agree on w constraints are not related by any reparameterization transformation — they are genuinely distinct functional representations.

The statement confuses empirical agreement (matching on finite data) with structural identity (being the same function up to parameter transformation). The former is a local condition on w points; the latter is a global functional relationship. This conflation is invalid.
key_assumption: "Candidates" refers to distinct neural network configurations (different widths, initializations, architectures) and "same numerical prediction" means identical outputs on the held-out constraint set within the 1e-3 tolerance specified in the experiment protocol.
